# iconlens

> Offline accessibility lint for standalone SVG files.

iconlens reads a standalone `.svg` file and computes the accessible name a screen reader would use, then reports the structural failures that remove it: missing alt text, dangling `aria-labelledby` references, and bad focus order. It lints the asset itself, with no browser and no live DOM.

It runs entirely offline, with no network calls and no telemetry, and can read from standard input. Output is human-readable text, stable JSON (one object for a single file, an array for many), and SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning. Exit codes are `0` (no findings at or above `--fail-on`), `1` (findings), `2` (invalid usage or an input that is not well-formed SVG), and `3` (I/O error).

## Docs
- [Overview](https://srivtx.github.io/iconlens/): Catch inaccessible SVG before it ships, with an in-browser playground.
- [Rules](https://srivtx.github.io/iconlens/rules): The eight rules and how the accessible name of a standalone SVG is computed.
- [Usage](https://srivtx.github.io/iconlens/usage): CLI flags, exit codes, JSON output, and the TypeScript library API.
- [CI](https://srivtx.github.io/iconlens/ci): SARIF 2.1.0 output for GitHub code scanning and an exit-code gate for pull requests.
- [FAQ](https://srivtx.github.io/iconlens/faq): Scope, limitations, and comparisons to svglint, svgo, Biome, axe-core, and the W3C ACT rule.

## Optional
- [Source](https://github.com/srivtx/iconlens): TypeScript implementation, tests, and issue tracker.
- [Install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivtx/iconlens/main/install.sh): One-line install of the `iconlens` binary.
